dedupe_keys.name: ams ix peering platform outages from switching loops 2015 2022 and 2023

description: This post-event and operations case brings together three outages of the peering platform of the Amsterdam Internet Exchange, one of the largest internet exchanges in the world, all caused by layer-2 loops or leaks in the switching fabric. On 13 May 2015, around midday, a loop created during work on the platform dropped BGP sessions of connected networks for about an hour and caused connectivity problems across the Netherlands; AMS-IX blamed human error and said it would build a workflow to prevent a repeat. On 6 April 2022, from 10:20 to 10:45, an engineer preparing a routing test before planned maintenance set a wrong port configuration that created a loop, interrupting 74.5 per cent of BGP sessions on the platform. On 22 and 23 November 2023, in two windows, LACP frames from customer equipment leaked through a switch whose filter was not fully working; traffic fell to 2.1 Tb/s at worst and IPv4 BGP sessions from 885 to 550. After the last event AMS-IX applied filters to non-LACP links, changed provisioning, added alerts for problem frames and revised incident communication. Coverage: one exchange in Amsterdam, three events. Format and access: incident notices on the AMS-IX website and news reports, free. Caveats: the 2015 root-cause note went only to members; traffic effects outside the exchange were not measured here. Simulation uses: failure modes of shared switching fabrics, cascading loss of peering sessions and operational procedures at exchanges. Related records: the DE-CIX Frankfurt outage of 2018 and RIPE Atlas measurements show how traffic reroutes when an exchange fails.

name: AMS-IX peering platform outages from switching loops (2015, 2022 and 2023)

outcomes: Three loop or leak outages: about an hour in 2015, 74.5 per cent of BGP sessions lost for 25 minutes in 2022, traffic down to 2.1 Tb/s in 2023; filtering, provisioning and alerting were changed.
